svg.title: GPU memory hierarchy: closer to compute means faster and smaller
svg.text: GPU memory hierarchy: closer to compute = faster and smaller
Capacities for the report's RTX 4060 Laptop (Ada, AD107, 24 SMs), approximate; speeds as orders of magnitude
on-chip
Registers
private per thread; ~256 KB per SM, ~6 MB total; fastest (~1 clock cycle)
L1 cache / shared memory
~128 KB per SM (~3 MB total), shared by threads in an SM; tens of cycles
L2 cache
shared by the whole card; ~32 MB; one to two hundred cycles
Each SM (streaming multiprocessor) also holds CUDA cores and Tensor Cores;
registers and shared memory are the only fast storage programmers control.
Global memory = VRAM
here 8 GB GDDR6, ~256 GB/s; data-center cards use HBM (~3 TB/s order)
model weights and the KV cache live here; hundreds of cycles
System RAM (16 GB) ← PCIe 4.0 ×8, ~16 GB/s → graphics card
faster, smaller
bigger, slower
The misleading "local memory"
Despite the name, it is not on-chip:
when a thread runs out of registers,
extra variables "spill" into a
thread-private area of global memory,
helped only by the L1 / L2 caches.
So local memory is as slow as VRAM;
fast kernels avoid spilling.
